findings.issue_text: [High/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go DeleteCollection goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`, recording legacy delete-collection latency under the wrong metric

[High/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Create and Update storage-failure paths call `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)`, recording legacy duration for a legacy operation that never ran; should be `recordStorageDuration`

[Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Delete success path passes `name` as the kind label to `recordStorageDuration` instead of `options.Kind`, inconsistent with other call sites and breaking metric aggregation

[High/concurrency] dualwriter_mode3.go goroutines derive timeout contexts from the request ctx via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, so the async legacy write is aborted when the HTTP request completes; should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or a detached context

[Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Update passes raw `objInfo` to Legacy.Update instead of wrapping in `updateWrapper` as before, causing UpdatedObject to re-fetch from unified storage and risking stale data or double-applied transformations
[Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Create uses `options.Kind` for log/metric labels, but `metav1.CreateOptions.Kind` is typically empty, so metrics/logs lose the kind dimension
[Low/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go async paths only record legacy write errors in metrics and never log them, making dual-write drift undiagnosable

[Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go tests never assert `lsSpy.Counts("LegacyStorage.*")` nor synchronize on the async goroutine, so the legacy-write contract is untested and goroutines may race past test end
[Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go 'unified store fails' cases don't set up the legacy mock, so the unawaited goroutine may panic asynchronously on an unexpected mock call

[Low/bug] dualwriter_mode1_test.go / dualwriter_mode3_test.go removal of per-test `prometheus.NewRegistry()` and reuse of a shared package-level registry risks panics on duplicate metric registration across DualWriter instances
[Low/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go `setupLegacyFn` is never exercised (e.g., no legacy failure path test) and `wantErr` cases never verify which storage failed

[Low/bug] dualwriter_mode3_test.go TestMode3_Update sets a mock expectation invoked in an unsynchronized goroutine, making expectation verification impossible and risking races on the not-fully-goroutine-safe mock.Mock

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go DeleteCollection goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`, recording legacy delete-collection latency under the wrong metric

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the legacy write is performed in a goroutine (`d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`), but the latency/error is recorded via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of a legacy-specific metric recorder. This misattributes legacy delete-collection metrics to storage, matching the finding: `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` should be `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` (or equivalent).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Create and Update storage-failure paths call `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)`, recording legacy duration for a legacy operation that never ran; should be `recordStorageDuration`

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `startStorage` measures the unified storage `d.Storage.Create` call, but on error the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` before returning, even though no legacy operation ran. Similarly in `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the storage `Update` failure path logs the error and then calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)`. Both are mismatched metrics recording and should use `recordStorageDuration` for storage failures (as the success paths do).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Delete success path passes `name` as the kind label to `recordStorageDuration` instead of `options.Kind`, inconsistent with other call sites and breaking metric aggregation
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag the same inconsistency: metrics recording uses `name` as the kind/label argument instead of `options.Kind`, differing from other methods/call sites and leading to inconsistent metric aggregation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/concurrency] dualwriter_mode3.go goroutines derive timeout contexts from the request ctx via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, so the async legacy write is aborted when the HTTP request completes; should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or a detached context

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy operations are launched in goroutines (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) and each goroutine derives its context from the request-scoped ctx via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)`. Because the parent ctx is the request context, it will be canceled when the handler returns; since these goroutines are started right before returning, the derived context can be canceled immediately and the async legacy write/delete/update is likely aborted and never performed. This matches the finding; a detached context (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` + timeout) would be needed if the intent is to keep legacy writes running after the request finishes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Update passes raw `objInfo` to Legacy.Update instead of wrapping in `updateWrapper` as before, causing UpdatedObject to re-fetch from unified storage and risking stale data or double-applied transformations

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, the previous Update implementation computed the updated object once and then wrapped `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper` so both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update used the same already-updated object (avoiding running `UpdatedObject` twice). The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` and then (async) calls `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` without wrapping, so `UpdatedObjectInfo` may be evaluated independently for legacy, potentially applying non-idempotent transformations twice or producing divergent results between unified and legacy writes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go Create uses `options.Kind` for log/metric labels, but `metav1.CreateOptions.Kind` is typically empty, so metrics/logs lose the kind dimension

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the code sets log/metric labels using `options.Kind` (e.g., `d.Log.WithValues("kind", options.Kind, ...)` and `d.record*Duration(..., options.Kind, ...)`). The diff also shows multiple call sites/tests passing `&metav1.CreateOptions{}` (empty), which would make `options.Kind` an empty string and thus reduce the usefulness of logs/metrics for distinguishing kinds. This impacts observability/labeling rather than core correctness, and the diff does not prove any functional failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] dualwriter_mode3.go async paths only record legacy write errors in metrics and never log them, making dual-write drift undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are now performed in goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) and their errors are only passed into recordLegacyDuration(...) (or in DeleteCollection mistakenly recordStorageDuration(...)) with no log.Error(...) call. Previously, legacy errors were logged synchronously (e.g., "could not update object in legacy store"). This is a concrete observability regression for diagnosing legacy-write failures/drift, but it doesn’t by itself prove functional breakage from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go tests never assert `lsSpy.Counts("LegacyStorage.*")` nor synchronize on the async goroutine, so the legacy-write contract is untested and goroutines may race past test end

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy operations are now executed asynchronously in goroutines for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection (e.g., `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create(...) ... }()`). The new pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go tests do not synchronize with these goroutines (no wait/chan/AssertExpectations after ensuring the goroutine ran), and they also no longer assert legacy-call counts (they switched from spies to testify mocks but never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` or otherwise verify the legacy write happened). As a result, the legacy-write contract in Mode3 is effectively untested and the async goroutines can run after the test completes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go 'unified store fails' cases don't set up the legacy mock, so the unawaited goroutine may panic asynchronously on an unexpected mock call

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, the legacy write/delete/update/deletecollection calls are started in a goroutine only *after* the unified store operation succeeds. In the various "unified store fails" test cases (e.g., `TestMode3_Delete` error case, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` error case, `TestMode3_Update` error case), the unified store mock returns an error, so the function returns early and no legacy goroutine is launched—there’s no asynchronous legacy mock call to panic on. Therefore the finding’s stated scenario (failure cases causing an unmocked legacy goroutine call) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] dualwriter_mode1_test.go / dualwriter_mode3_test.go removal of per-test `prometheus.NewRegistry()` and reuse of a shared package-level registry risks panics on duplicate metric registration across DualWriter instances

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode1_test.go` the per-test `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` is removed while `NewDualWriter(..., p)` still uses `p`, implying a shared (likely package-level) Prometheus registry is now reused across multiple DualWriter instances/tests. If `NewDualWriter` registers collectors on the provided registry, reusing the same registry across tests can lead to duplicate-registration errors/panics. The diff shows the registry reuse pattern but does not show how `NewDualWriter` registers metrics, so the panic is a risk rather than a verifiable failure from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] dualwriter_mode3_test.go `setupLegacyFn` is never exercised (e.g., no legacy failure path test) and `wantErr` cases never verify which storage failed

adjudication.rationale: In the new `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` tests, error cases (e.g., `TestMode3_Get`, `TestMode3_List`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, `TestMode3_Update`) only assert `assert.Error(t, err)` and do not check that the failure originated from the unified store vs legacy store. Also, Mode3’s implementation performs legacy writes/deletes/updates asynchronously in goroutines (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection` in `dualwriter_mode3.go`), and the tests do not include any case where Storage succeeds but Legacy fails (nor do they assert that legacy calls happened), leaving the new async legacy-path behavior untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] dualwriter_mode3_test.go TestMode3_Update sets a mock expectation invoked in an unsynchronized goroutine, making expectation verification impossible and risking races on the not-fully-goroutine-safe mock.Mock

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Update() performs the Legacy.Update call inside a new goroutine (with a timeout). In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go TestMode3_Update sets a testify/mock expectation for LegacyStorage.Update, but the test does not synchronize/wait for that goroutine nor call AssertExpectations, so the legacy expectation may never be observed before the test completes (and the mock may be accessed after the subtest returns), leading to unverifiable expectations and potential race/flakiness under concurrency/race detection.
